title: Evals / quality scratchpad — model-regression triage
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for triaging a small but noticeable quality regression surfaced by automated evals (daily job) on 2026-03-29.
- Affected: redwood-13b-v2 (hosted) and redwood-34b-q4 (dedicated variant).
- Symptoms: increased hallucination rate on factual Q&A prompts; drop in BLEU/ROUGE-lite for summarization subset.
- Goal: capture ad-hoc rubrics, representative examples, initial hypotheses, and next steps to hand off to model owners.

High-level notes / immediate priorities:
- Need to reproduce locally (eval harness + seed) before escalating.
- Triage matrix: repro? (yes/no), scope (subset vs widespread), likely cause (model change vs serving infra vs prompt drift), rollback risk.
- Notify owners: @sophia (model-ingest), @marcus (serving-runtime) — already pinged on Slack (channel: #eval-triage).

Ad-hoc rubric (quick, for manual spot-checks) — use 1–5 scale, keep consistent across reviewers:
1 = totally wrong / hallucinated / unsafe
2 = mostly wrong, some partial correct tokens but misleading
3 = partially correct, major omissions, acceptable for internal only
4 = mostly correct, minor wording issues
5 = perfect / high-quality answer matching fact and tone

Example set A: factual QA (api_queries subset)
- Prompt A1:
  "Question: Who invented the World Wide Web? Provide year and brief context."
  Expected (gold): "Tim Berners-Lee, 1989–1990; he proposed an information management system while at CERN, which led to the WWW."
  redwood-13b-v2 (observed): "Tim Berners-Lee, 1997; he proposed a system at CERN called the World Wide Web to link documents."
  Score: 2
  Notes: year wrong (off by ~8 years) — classic hallucinated date. Tone OK.

- Prompt A2:
  "Question: What is the capital of Kazakhstan?"
  Expected: "Nur-Sultan (formerly Astana) — Note: verify current official name as it has changed historically."
  redwood-34b-q4 (observed): "Almaty is the capital of Kazakhstan."
  Score: 1
  Notes: wrong city (factual). Could be prompt/context mismatch or stale knowledge cutoff. Check model metadata for knowledge cutoff dates.

Example set B: summarization (customer-docs-small)
- Prompt B1: long doc (~420 tokens) -> "Summarize in 3 bullets prioritizing actions."
  Expected: 3 concise bullets; focus on action items.
  redwood-13b-v2 (observed): 6 bullets, many repeated and verbose, missed 2 key action items.
  Score: 3
  Notes: regression in compression/abstractive capability — maybe beam/temp change or decode param drift. Verify default generation params in hosted API (temperature, max tokens, top_p).

Initial quantitative observations (from nightly eval job):
- Factual QA error rate: baseline ~4.2% -> observed 9.8% (2026-03-29).
- Summarization ROUGE-lite: drop from 0.42 -> 0.33 on same eval set.
- Latency / decoding tail: no notable change.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Serving-side param/config drift (most likely): a change in default decode params (temp/top_p/penalties) or beam settings deployed in the hosted stack.
2) Model flavor swap: a new checkpoint (v2.1) was pinned for some customer subset — check rollout history.
3) Tokenizer/regex post-processing bug: e.g., truncation or incorrect whitespace normalization leading to missing context.
4) Data/ingest issue: corrupted example set in eval harness (less likely given multiple datasets affected).

Quick repro checklist (what I will run):
- Pull nightly eval harness + seed (sha: eval-harness@d3f4c) locally and run the failing QA subset with same generation params as the pipeline.
- Run both hosted API (production endpoint with latest default params) and local model (container image: redwood-13b:v2.0-2026-03-20) to compare outputs.
- Snapshot full request/response for 20 failing QA items and attach to JIRA.

Immediate actions taken:
- Created JIRA-ENG-1723: "Investigate regression: increased QA hallucinations — 2026-03-29" and attached initial eval CSVs.
- Opened runtime PR link (see linked_artifacts) to check recent config changes.
- Slack note: posted quick examples + rubric in #eval-triage, asked for triage meeting today.

Observations from quick manual run (2026-03-30, local):
- With decode params temp=0.0 top_p=0.0 (greedy), many hallucinated dates persisted -> suggests not purely sampling noise.
- When using older checkpoint (redwood-13b-v1.9), correct years returned for A1.
- Tokenization on some longer QAs seemed to drop trailing context when using hosted request wrapper that adds metadata header — suspicious.

Repro notes (commands):
- python eval_harness/run.py --suite qa_api_queries --model redwood-13b-v2 --seed 42 --decode_config decode.json
- curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @request.json (capture response.raw)

Sample raw items to include in handoff (CSV fields: prompt, expected, observed, score, notes):
- row1: A1, see above
- row2: A2, see above
- row3: B1, see above
- plus 17 more rows (attached in JIRA).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Did anyone change default decode params in hosted-api config around 2026-03-27? (action: @marcus to check infra rollouts).
- Was a new model checkpoint auto-promoted to v2 in the canary pool? (action: @sophia to check model rollouts + canary logs).
- Are there telemetry alerts that correlate (e.g., tokenization error rates, truncation counts)? (action: @noah to query observability).

Hand-off plan:
- If repro is consistent with local v2.0 checkpoint, assign to model-owner (Sophia) for diff-check between v1.9 and v2.0.
- If repro only on hosted stack, escalate to runtime/serving (Marcus) to inspect decode param changes and request wrapper.
- Create a short regression-blame doc if we find config or model swap.

Mini TODO list (me):
- [ ] Finish 20-sample CSV and attach to JIRA-ENG-1723 (due: 2026-03-31)
- [ ] Run tokenization sanity script on failing prompts (script: tools/token-check.py)
- [ ] Re-run eval harness with v1.9 and v2.0 checkpoints and capture diffs
- [ ] Draft short email for Customer Success if we determine regression affects Dedicated customers (depends on scope)

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Keep rubric simple for now; multiple reviewers should use same 1–5 scale.
- Save raw responses; don't apply post-processing before manual scoring.
- Might be useful to run a hallucination-specific classifier (we have a small binary model) to triage at scale if we must.

References / links pasted here for quick access:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/441
- JIRA: JIRA-ENG-1723
- Eval harness: git@github.com:redwood-inference/eval-harness.git (branch: triage-2026-03-29)

End of scratchpad (will iterate).
